ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a gray triangle, and there is a white circle at each of the three vertices of the triangle. The center of each circle is at the corresponding vertex of the triangle, so the white parts covered by the circles inside the triangle are respectively three sectors whose central angles are the interior angles of the triangle. Reasoning: Let the three interior angles of the triangle be A, B, C, then A+B+C=180°. The radius of each circle is 2 m, so the total area of the three removed sectors is ((A+B+C)/360°)·π·2^2 = (180/360)·4π = 2π. The total area of the triangle is 80 m², therefore the area of the gray region is 80-2π.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a grey triangular region with three unshaded circular sectors removed at the triangle's vertices, one sector from each circle. Let the triangle's interior angles be A, B, and C. From the text, the full triangle area is 80 m^2 and each circle has radius 2 m. The removed area inside the triangle is the sum of three sectors with central angles A, B, and C. Since A+B+C=180 degrees, the total removed sector area is (180/360)·π·2^2 = 2π. Subtract this from the triangle area to get the grey area: 80 - 2π.
